candidate.build: CUDA 13.1, sm_89, FP64. New radiation units -O2 --fmad=false. Unchanged fast-compile gas objects reused; no claim of fully optimized gas end-to-end performance.

mathematics: Original table interpolation, phase balancing, angular quadrature, cell-order upwind Gauss-Seidel arithmetic, source relaxation and convergence tolerances retained.

Sequential angular updates use the latest preceding directions; requested parallel angles retain frozen sources and now execute independent directions on CUDA streams. No mesh/case specialization or CPU fallback.
Device stopping flags freeze the first converged iterate within bounded ordinary CUDA graph batches. The two generic angular scheduling modes share the same cell arithmetic.
Original bounded material equilibrium/implicit roots and conservative boundary energy scaling moved to shared host/device math; GPU ordered transaction sums retain native summation order.
Phase storage is linear in cells times directions, reconstructing balanced probabilities in the original product order.
remaining_host_work: OpenFOAM geometry extraction, dependency-plan construction and boundary/metadata policy.
Canonical snapshot clamping, state/result mirrors, native field publication and ordered integrated diagnostic sums.
Layer five geometry and full application integration are unfinished; this is not a fully resident five-layer chain.

limitations: A 32^3 full CHT case exceeds the original absolute global energy/mass test bounds on both baseline and candidate: 0.0023011565 J and 2.9366345e-9 kg. All output fields, particle checkpoints and residuals are unchanged by migration. This case is marked BASELINE_ABSOLUTE_CONSERVATION_BOUNDS_EXCEEDED, not an absolute-conservation pass.

Component balances locate that residual in the existing gas update: gas 0.002301204267 J, solid 2.12252611e-8 J, particle radiation 7.40080219e-12 J, identical CPU/GPU. The migrated radiation and solid exchanges close within the original test bound.

Existing mobile radiation uses configured constant heat factor, while particle enthalpy uses a nonlinear law. Both transaction-model and nonlinear-enthalpy inventories are retained; small-case nonlinear drift 0.0007710456848 J is unchanged, not claimed to be zero.

Native restarts reconstruct calculated particle boundary outputs differently from continuous runs. Internal physical fields remain within tolerance, restarted CPU/GPU fields and particle checkpoints match; boundary differences and tiny native enthalpy-carry roundoff are explicitly recorded.

Early conditional graph upwind experiments matched ordinary numerical tests but produced unresolved ComputeSanitizer CUDA999/OOB reports. Production layer-four upwind uses ordinary graphs, with final unit/native/full-app memcheck zero errors. The rejected experiment is not claimed to be a sanitizer bug.

Unreproducible nvcc/GCC internal compiler errors also occurred while compiling unchanged baseline sources; successful bounded retries retained. No unrelated hardware investigation or runtime fallback was added.
